output.myth: Sarra was the best fighting kite on the Leeward shore. She had a tail of knotted sailcloth and a bridle nobody could bend, and every spring she cut the lines of every kite in the bay. Tavo the Gale liked her and blew her higher than any kite had gone. One calm evening a boy from across the harbour, too proud to lose, threw his line up under hers. She turned to cut him, and the wind dropped. Her string went slack, then taut, and Tavo laughed, and it snapped at the knot. We watched her climb into the Upper Sea, a small dark diamond with her tail trailing light. Hesk counted her and found her missing. Aun says he waved to her from the cut edge of the sky, but Aun says many things. Her string still drifts out past the Lamp Road. If your kite tangles, say her name and let go the line.
output.verse:
Sarra's string snapped clean,
the Gale laughed, the wind fell low,
still she drifts, unreeled.
